=== file-001.md ===
Homeward

The train exhales beside the river road,
Low windows kindle one by one in gold.
Leaves gather softly at the garden gate,
And chimney smoke arrives before the late.
The hedges wear a russet, windblown crown,
While dusk unbuttons all the sleeping town.

My key remembers turning in the door;
Warm lamplight pools across the wooden floor.
The kettle hums, the hallway holds my name,
And rain taps gently on the darkened pane.

Outside, the branches bow and shadows roam;
Inside, the evening folds me into home.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward

The last train sighs beyond the hill,
I turn where porch lights gather gold.
Leaves murmur along the curb,
Each window keeps a small warm story.
My key remembers the faithful lock,
Smoke lifts softly from the chimneys.
The hallway carries cedar and bread,
And shadows loosen from my coat.
Behind me, the street grows quiet,
Before me, the kettle starts to sing.
I cross the threshold, breathing deep,
And night becomes a room of welcome.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward Glow

The last bus sighs beneath a copper sky,
Leaves gather softly at the curbside grate.
My key is warm between my fingers now,
And window light has learned to watch for me.
The porch boards answer with their weathered song,
Smoke curls like a letter from the chimney.
Inside, the kettle hums against the dusk,
My coat releases rain and distant streets.
The rooms receive me with their patient hush,
A lamp pools gold across the kitchen floor.
Beyond the glass, the branches loosen stars;
I close the door and let the night come in.

=== file-001.md ===
Threshold Light

The road unspools beneath a copper sky,
Wet leaves gather at the gate like letters.
My key finds its old familiar star,
And window-glow spills softly through the curtains.
The kettle's hush remembers how to sing,
While boots release the weather by the door.
A woodsmoke breath drifts down the quiet hall,
And supper's warmth is waiting in the walls.
Outside, bare branches write against the dusk;
Inside, each room restores its gentle name.
I set my traveling silence on the table,
Then hear the house say: you are here again.

=== file-001.md ===
Hearthward

Maples burn low beside the lane,
Rain gathers on the garden gate.
My keys remember every turn,
The porch light holds its patient gold.
A chimney writes across the dusk,
Smoke soft as wool above the roof.
Inside, the kettle starts to sing,
And cedar warms the narrow hall.
I leave the day beside the door,
Its scattered leaves upon the mat.
The windows bloom with amber peace,
And home receives me, whole and still.

=== file-001.md ===
Autumn Return

The road unspools beneath a copper sky,
and maples kindle softly by the lane.
My window gathers dusk; the swallows fly
like loosened stitches through the evening rain.
The porch light blooms before I reach the gate,
a small, warm star against the cooling blue.
The door remembers how to ease its weight;
the hall holds cedar, bread, and something true.
Inside, the kettle starts its patient song,
while wind combs gold from every waiting tree.
I set my travel-worn heart down where it belongs,
and autumn closes gently over me.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward in October

The last bus sighs beneath a saffron sky,
And wind unbuttons gold from every tree.
I follow puddles holding scraps of light
Past chimneys breathing cedar into dusk.
The windows of my house bloom one by one,
Small planets warm against the cooling blue.
At my approach, the gate remembers me;
Its iron latch gives softly in my hand.
Inside, the kettle gathers up its song,
And woolen shadows settle by the fire.
I leave the evening folded on the step
And find my name waiting in the lamplight.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward Through October

The last gold leaf turns softly in the lane,
Rain holds the amber windows in its palm.
I cross the dusk beneath a woolen sky,
While chimney smoke unwinds its thread of calm.
The gate remembers every hand and step,
The porch light gathers shadows at the door.
Inside, the kettle hums a small, bright hymn,
And cedar breathes from old familiar drawers.
My coat releases weather to the chair,
The clock resumes its patient, kindly chime.
Beyond the glass, the dark keeps falling leaves;
Within, my name is warmed by fire and time.

=== file-001.md ===
Lanterns at the Gate

The road folds gold beneath the thinning trees,
and woodsmoke gathers softly in the blue.
My footsteps wake the fallen leaves like seas
that whisper every distant mile I knew.
At last, the windows hold their squares of flame;
the porch remembers creak and weathered rain.
A kettle sings the small, familiar name
of evening settling warmly through the pane.
I leave the wind to comb the darkened hill,
unlace the day, and hear the hallway breathe.
Home opens like a hand grown kind and still,
with apple light caught trembling in its leaves.

=== file-001.md ===
Returning by Amber Light

The road unspools beneath a russet sky,
and woodsmoke gathers softly in the cold.
Each window blooms a small and steady gold,
while maples let their copper syllables fly.
My boots remember every weathered stone,
the gate’s familiar creak, the low stone wall.
The garden leans, leaf-laden, toward the fall,
and dusk lays down its scarf across the lawn.
Inside, the kettle starts its silver song;
a lamp receives my shadow at the door.
The year grows quiet, asking nothing more—
I breathe, and all the wandering comes along.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward at Dusk

Maples burn softly along the lane,
Rain-bright windows gather the gold.
My footsteps loosen the day’s old chain,
While chimney smoke curls blue in the cold.

A blackbird settles beneath the eaves,
The gate knows well the touch of my hand.
Warm light trembles through russet leaves,
And supper’s fragrance crosses the land.

Inside, the clock keeps its patient tune,
Coats bloom on hooks by the polished door.
Night rises gently, a harvest moon,
And home becomes my whole world once more.

=== file-001.md ===
Autumn Threshold

The last gold leaf turns softly in the lane,
Smoke folds blue above the neighboring eaves.
My key is warm against my palm again,
While dusk collects its amber, drifting leaves.

The windows hold a welcome in their glow,
And cinnamon and rain breathe through the hall.
I set the day down gently in the low
Hush of familiar shadows on the wall.

Outside, the wind rehearses winter's tune;
Inside, the kettle hums, the fire sighs.
Home gathers round me like a tender moon,
And evening settles kindly in my eyes.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward Through October

The dusk folds gold along the sleeping lane,
I carry woodsmoke softly in my coat.
Red leaves gather at the garden gate,
Like little boats that know the way to float.

One window kindles amber through the rain,
The kettle hums its welcome from within.
My footsteps loosen from the day's long miles,
And evening draws its woolen quiet in.

The porch light holds a circle on the stone,
The maples breathe against the darkening blue.
I turn the key, and all the world grows warm:
Autumn has brought me home to you.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward at Dusk

The maples burn beside the quiet lane,
And cider-colored light fills every pane.
I leave the restless city’s silver hum,
While chimney smoke says softly, “You have come.”

Wet leaves gather under my unhurried feet,
The evening folds its gold around the street.
A lamp blooms warm behind the curtained glass,
As swallows stitch the dark above the grass.

The door knows well the turning of my key,
The kettle sings a small, familiar plea.
In autumn’s hush, the wandering world grows still—
I am returned, and all the rooms are filled.

=== file-001.md ===
Autumn Threshold

The train sighs softly at the edge of town,
And maple leaves turn copper in the rain.
I follow windowlight through streets gone brown,
Past chimney smoke and gardens hushed again.
The dusk has folded gold beneath its wing,
While sparrows stitch the dark from eave to eave.
My key is warm, a small and shining thing,
The porch lamp glows among the fallen leaves.
Inside, the kettle hums its welcome tune,
And woolen rooms hold daylight's fading fire.
I hang the evening by the crescent moon,
Then come home wholly, heart and coat and mire.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward Through October

The last bus sighs beneath the amber trees,
and rain-dark pavement holds the fading sky.
I carry dusk like apples in my sleeves,
while chimney smoke unthreads the evening high.

At every gate, the wind remembers names;
the maples lay their small red hands on stone.
A kitchen window gathers gold from flames,
and makes the waiting street feel less alone.

My key turns softly in the weathered door;
warm bread and cedar meet me in the hall.
The world grows quiet on the rugs and floor,
and autumn folds its wings around us all.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward in Autumn

The dusk folds amber through the thinning trees,
A chimney writes its welcome in the blue;
Dry leaves go whispering along my knees,
And every lane remembers what I knew.

The river holds one last unbroken gleam,
While windows kindle gold behind the rain;
The fields, half-mist, grow tender as a dream,
And crows draw darkened stitches through the plain.

At last the gate gives softly to my hand,
The porch light warms the gathering evening's hem;
I cross the threshold into lamp-lit land,
And autumn, breathing, settles over them.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward at Dusk

Amber leaves gather along the lane,
The windows kindle through misty rain.
My footsteps soften on cedar ground,
Where chimney smoke makes a silver sound.
The day folds down in a russet shawl,
And crows write shadows across the wall.
A lamp in the kitchen calls me near,
Warm as a hand, bright as a dear.
I leave the wind at the painted door,
And hear old floorboards welcome once more.
Outside, the maples burn low and gold;
Inside, the evening loosens its hold.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward in Amber

The road unspools beneath a russet sky,
Leaves gather gold along the quiet lane.
Woodsmoke lifts its small, familiar sigh,
And evening taps like rain against the pane.
The porch light blooms before the daylight goes,
A harbor bright beyond the darkening field.
My footsteps stir the fragrance of the rose
That frost will keep but never wholly shield.
Inside, the kettle hums a gentle tune,
Old clocks make islands of their measured chime.
I hang the wind beside the crescent moon,
And let the warm rooms take me out of time.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward Embers

The maples kindle softly by the lane,
While dusk folds gold beneath a violet sky.
My shoes remember every shining drain,
And chimney smoke draws welcome from on high.

A kettle hums behind the window glass;
The porch light gathers moths like drifting snow.
I hear the garden's last brown whisper pass,
Then turn the latch I have always known.

Inside, the rooms are warm with bread and rain;
The evening settles, amber, at my door.
I set my wandering heart down once again,
And autumn finds me safely home once more.

=== file-001.md ===
Autumn’s Welcome

The amber dusk unbuttons from the sky,
And leaves drift softly past the garden gate.
My window kindles gold against the rye,
While chimney smoke curls warmly as I wait.
The path remembers every tired shoe,
Its puddles holding fragments of the moon.
A kettle sings the evening slowly through,
And cedar shadows gather in the room.
I hang the day beside the old brass key,
Then breathe the apple-scented, cooling air.
Home opens like a lantern just for me,
With firelight folding peace into each chair.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward Ember

The road wears copper beneath my feet,
and maples kindle the cooling air.
Windows bloom with a softened gold
where evening gathers in every square.

My coat holds smoke and orchard wind,
the day’s last crow calls from a wire.
Beyond the gate, the porch lamp wakes,
a small, unshaken amber fire.

I turn the key; warm voices rise,
with cinnamon, rain, and woolen light.
The season folds its russet wings,
and home receives the falling night.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward Ember

Maples burn softly along the lane,
Rain-polished windows gather gold;
My footsteps loosen the day’s last chain,
While chimney smoke climbs blue and cold.
The gate remembers my waiting hand,
The porch light warms the evening air;
Dry leaves whisper across the land,
And supper’s promise meets me there.
A kettle sings beyond the door,
Familiar shadows cross the floor;
I bring the dusk in on my sleeve,
And rest beneath the russet eve.

=== file-001.md ===
Autumn's Return

The last gold leaf turns softly in the lane,
Blue dusk gathers at the garden gate;
I carry woodsmoke home like a refrain,
While windows kindle, warm and small and late.

The porch light blooms against the cooling air,
And apples breathe their sweetness from the bowl;
A woolen hush waits patiently upstairs,
The house remembering the shape of soul.

Beyond the glass, the evening crows depart,
Their dark wings folding into amber foam;
I set my weary footsteps by the hearth,
And find the season waiting: welcome home.

=== file-001.md ===
Lanterns at the Gate

Amber leaves whirl along the lane,
The dusk folds blue around the hill;
Smoke from chimneys scents the rain,
And every window waits me still.

My boots remember every stone,
The garden bends with russet fire;
Behind the door, the house’s tone
Is kettle-song and lamp-lit choir.

I cross the threshold, warm and slow,
While twilight settles on the eaves;
Home gathers me from wind and glow,
And night comes softly through the leaves.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward at Dusk

The maples burn softly along the lane,
their copper leaves loosening into rain.
One window glows through the gathering blue,
a small, steadfast star I have traveled to.
The gate knows the weight of my lingering hand;
the porch boards answer, warm as remembered land.
Inside, cinnamon, wool, and the hiss of the kettle
make the whole tired world suddenly gentle.
My coat sheds twilight beside the door,
and silence opens its familiar floor.
Beyond the glass, the first cold wind may roam—
but evening folds around me, and I am home.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward, Under October

At dusk, the maples gather fire along the lane.
My footsteps stir a small republic of leaves.
The river keeps its copper counsel beyond the fields,
while chimney smoke unthreads the cooling blue.
A single window kindles at the hill's low shoulder,
gold as bread, and just as welcome from afar.
The gate remembers the pressure of my hand.
In the garden, asters bow beneath their silver breath.
Then the familiar door gives way to lamplight,
to apples, wool, and rain asleep upon the coat.
Outside, the dark folds up the wandering road;
inside, my name is waiting in the quiet.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward at Dusk

The maples loosen copper into the lane,
and rain remembers every window's glow.
My footsteps gather softly at the gate,
where chimney smoke is knitting up the blue.
The porch lamp pours its honey on the steps,
and somewhere bread is warming in the dark.
I hear the kettle thinking of a song,
the old clock keeping amber in its throat.
The rooms receive the evening from my coat,
their shadows opening like familiar hands.
Outside, the last leaf turns upon the wind;
inside, my name becomes a fire again.

=== file-001.md ===
The Road Knows My Name

Maples kindle softly along the lane,
and dusk folds blue around the fields.
My boots remember each familiar stone;
the old gate loosens its small, warm sigh.
Smoke rises from the chimney like a prayer
the wind has carried faithfully all day.
Behind the glass, a lamp keeps watch for me,
gold pooled against the gathering rain.
The door opens before I lift my hand,
and every shadow learns the shape of welcome.
Autumn leaves its rustling at the threshold;
inside, my heart hangs up its coat.

=== file-001.md ===
The Way Back

At dusk, the maples lift their lanterned hands,
and cider-colored light pools on the lane.
My footsteps stir the hush of fallen leaves;
each small crackle knows and says my name.
The chimneys braid blue smoke into the cold,
while windows bloom like hearths along the hill.
I pass the gate where summer's roses slept
and feel the turning year grow kind and still.
Then home appears, its porch lamp held aloft,
a star made warm enough for human weather.
I cross the threshold, carrying the dusk,
and all the scattered parts of me come together.
